# BeyondRetarget and Two-Stage Redirection: How to Compare, and What Are the Advantages

> Update: 2026-10-18. The values and comparison demonstrations on this page are from the author's paper and project pages; this tutorial has not yet run the four baselines again. What we have successfully executed is still [ six-second online reasoning ](results/validation.md). Below, the interpretation of the paper results and the process of running it again with a video are explained separately.

## 1. First, distinguish between "replacing robots" and "changing methods"

The same action drives eight robots, demonstrating the cross-body adaptability. To compare the algorithms, first fix them as **Unitree G1 with 29 joints**, and have each production line receive the same video segment:

| Method | Video to robot motion trajectory | Key comparison points |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GVHMR → GMR | Video → Human motion estimation → Optimized redirection | How human estimation error affects geometric matching |
| GVHMR → NMR | Same GVHMR human estimation → Learned redirection | Fixed human estimation, only different redirection methods |
| WHAM → GMR | Video → Another human motion estimation → Optimized redirection | Fixed redirection method, only different human estimation |
| WHAM → NMR | Same WHAM human estimation → Learned redirection | Whether the results depend on a specific human estimator |
| BeyondRetarget | Video features → Shared motion representation → G1 decoding and post-processing | Direct generation of robot trajectories with overall effectiveness |

Here, [GVHMR](https://github.com/zju3dv/GVHMR) and [WHAM](https://github.com/yohanshin/WHAM) are responsible for restoring human movement; [GMR](https://github.com/YanjieZe/GMR) and [NMR](https://github.com/NJU3DV-HumanoidGroup/MakeTrackingEasy) are responsible for converting human movements into robot movements. Human animations output by GVHMR alone cannot be compared with the robot animations produced by BeyondRetarget as a complete method.

This 2x2 design helps identify the issues: improvement occurs after changing the human body estimator, suggesting that upstream reconstruction may be a bottleneck; no change is observed in input human body estimation, but improvement occurs after changing the redirector, indicating that the mapping method matters. However, these observations are still influenced by factors such as models, configurations, and post-processing, and no causal conclusions can be drawn based on individual observations alone.

## 2. First, look at the comparisons already published by the author

### 2.1 Quantitative Results: Comparison on the Same G1

The following excerpt is from [BeyondRetarget paper v1 Table 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29850v1#S4.T1). **These are not the results measured again in this tutorial**. MAMPJPE represents the key point error after shape alignment, RTE is the root trajectory error, and FS is the horizontal foot slide of the support frame; the three items are better when they are smaller. The execution success rate was evaluated using the author’s SONIC tracking metrics.

| Method of RGB Input | MAMPJPE ↓ (mm) | RTE ↓ (mm) | FS ↓ (mm/frame) | Successful Segments / Total Segments ↑ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GVHMR → NMR | 39.19 | 701.13 | 2.28 | 340 / 362 |
| GVHMR → GMR | 39.46 | 637.33 | 3.30 | 313 / 362 |
| WHAM → NMR | 43.15 | 849.36 | 6.64 | 342 / 362 |
| WHAM → GMR | 45.88 | 217.76 | 13.30 | 295 / 362 |
| **BeyondRetarget** | **26.36** | **80.74** | **1.71** | **347 / 362** |

Among these four RGB baselines, the lowest MAMPJPE is 39.19 mm; BeyondRetarget's 26.36 mm is **32.7% lower**, calculated as `(39.19 - 26.36) / 39.19`. The execution success rate ranges from the best 342/362 to 347/362, which is **94.48% → 95.86%, an increase of about 1.38 percentage points**. These comparisons are based on the best baseline for each metric, and not all improvements can be attributed to a single opponent.

The paper also sets two diagnostic baselines for **GT Human Movement → Redirection**, to bypass human estimation errors; they have additional truth value information and do not participate in the RGB method ranking:

| Diagnostic methods using human body true values | MAMPJPE ↓ (mm) | RTE ↓ (mm) | FS ↓ (mm/frame) | Successful segments / Total segments ↑ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GT → NMR | 33.26 | 837.62 | 1.30 | 346 / 362 |
| GT → GMR | 32.02 | 36.01 | 0.82 | 347 / 362 |

Therefore, the conclusion should be limited to: **In the author’s RGB input evaluation, the results of BeyondRetarget are better than those of the four two-stage baselines; it does not outperform all settings and metrics.** For example, the root trajectory error and foot slip in GT → GMR are lower, and the number of successful executions is the same as that of BeyondRetarget. The lower shape alignment pose error cannot be interpreted as a more accurate human motion restoration from the video compared to the human body true value.

### 2.2 Official Demo: Viewing with Questions

Open the synchronization comparison video provided by the following author; these are **official qualitative demonstrations, not the baseline results we generated this time**:

- [ Crossing the arms and swinging the arm ](https://bear-ty.github.io/Beyondretarget_page/assets/videos/main-result-waist-arm-swing.mp4): Check whether the elbows and hands remain in their corresponding positions, and if there are any posture changes during intense movement.
- [ Putting both hands behind the back ](https://bear-ty.github.io/Beyondretarget_page/assets/videos/main-result-behind-back.mp4): Determine whether the hands are in front of or behind the torso; it is easy to miss depth issues by only looking at the front profile.
- [ Large-scale arm rotation ](https://bear-ty.github.io/Beyondretarget_page/assets/videos/main-result-large-arm-circle.mp4): Observe the direction of the shoulders and elbows and the continuity of movement, not just whether the robot is "moving".
- [ Raising hands and squatting ](https://bear-ty.github.io/Beyondretarget_page/assets/videos/main-result-hand-raise-squat-five-methods.mp4): Observe the upper limbs, waist, and feet simultaneously to avoid focusing only on a visually pleasing frame.

Links and descriptions are from the [ official project page ](https://bear-ty.github.io/Beyondretarget_page/). These are cases selected by the author to explain various failure modes. They cannot replace the statistical results of a complete test set. The six-second low-resolution input actions in this chapter are simple, and they are not suitable for highlighting the advantages of a certain method based solely on visual perception.

## 3. Why direct prediction of robot actions may be better

The two-stage approach first fits the human body, and then passes this result to the redirector. In the second stage, the original image is not visible: if the hand behind the body is estimated in front of the body upstream, geometric matching later may faithfully reproduce this error. Even if the human posture is correct, the proportions between the human and robot limbs, joint structure, and reachable space are different, and mapping errors may still occur.

BeyondRetarget uses the final robot output as a learning objective, enabling the visual representation to serve the target ontology; the robot-specific resolution dock and contact correction reprocessing handle shape and support issues. This provides a mechanism for reducing the accumulation of errors across stages, but "one fewer intermediate representation" does not guarantee superiority over any two-stage method. The advantages still need to be tested under the same task, input, and computational conditions.

Post-contact processing also involves trade-offs. In Table 3 of the paper, the MAMPJPE with refinement removed is 25.73 mm, and the full model is 26.36 mm; meanwhile, FS decreases from 4.51 to 1.71 mm/frame, and the contact misalignment rate drops from 22.18% to 6.17%. This indicates that the correction sacrifices some posture alignment in exchange for more stable contact. "More like joints" and "easier to execute" should not be considered as the same goal. [ Source: Paper ablation table ](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.29850v1#S4.T3)

## 4. Re-run by oneself: First connect GVHMR → GMR

This is the most suitable local baseline to be updated first, as GMR has provided a formal entry to read the GVHMR output. Below are the steps for verification according to the upstream source code. **This tutorial has not yet executed the entire process.**

### 4.1 Install independently and record the version

Prepare independent environments, reasoning weights, and authorized human models for [GVHMR installation documentation ](https://github.com/zju3dv/GVHMR/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) and [GMR installation documentation ](https://github.com/YanjieZe/GMR#installation), respectively. These are not the dependencies that are already present by default in the BeyondRetarget environment. The human models of GVHMR and the file extensions and directories required by GMR may differ; configure them according to the upstream instructions.

The version verified on this page is as follows; this is only the command verification version, not the complete baseline version used by the paper author at that time:

| Item | Verification Submission |
| --- | --- |
| GVHMR | `ee960bb6e2ea2d381aa97f08e9b71ef320b624b1` |
| GMR | `bb1bbe40774794fceb2a7c579a3464a28e68c844` |
| NMR | `ba87ad6541f6512df9a370acdd2c2d95da7ae419` |

For each project, use `git checkout <对应提交>` as a fixed version in the root directory of its repository, and save `git rev-parse HEAD`, environment dependency list, weight hash, and model hash. The upstream versions will change, so do not simply write "latest version" when displaying the results.

### 4.2 Using the Exactly Same Video

Execute in the root directory of the GVHMR project after activating its environment. `-s` indicates a static camera; it is assumed that the input also comes from a fixed position:

```bash
python tools/demo/demo.py --video=/absolute/path/person_6s.mp4 -s
```

It should get `outputs/demo/person_6s/hmr4d_results.pt`. After switching to the root directory of the GMR project and activating its environment:

```bash
python scripts/gvhmr_to_robot.py \
  --gvhmr_pred_file /absolute/path/GVHMR/outputs/demo/person_6s/hmr4d_results.pt \
  --robot unitree_g1 \
  --save_path /absolute/path/runs/comparison/gvhmr_gmr_g1.pkl \
  --record_video
```

This entry will open the viewer, requiring an available graphical environment. The video paths for version verification are generated by scripts under `videos/`, and there is no separate `--video_path` parameter; for batch experiments, the corresponding videos should be archived after each run to prevent overlapping outputs with the same name. To measure processing speed, do not enable the `--rate_limit` that imposes artificial speed limits. [ Source: GMR's GVHMR entry ](https://github.com/YanjieZe/GMR/blob/bb1bbe40774794fceb2a7c579a3464a28e68c844/scripts/gvhmr_to_robot.py)

### 4.3 Two export details that cause distortion in comparison

In the `gvhmr_to_robot.py` of the above GMR version:

- In MuJoCo, `qpos` uses wxyz, but `root_rot` saved in PKL is converted to **xyzw**. `root_rot_quat` in BeyondRetarget is **wxyz**; explicit adjustments are required during adaptation, not just changing the field name. The joint order of GMR also needs to be checked against the model.
- The main loop first adds 1 to 0 for `i` and then processes that frame, thus skipping frame 0. For formal comparison, the loop should be modified to process all frames and record the changes, or the missing first frame should be clearly marked based on the actual timestamp; the output with one fewer frame cannot be played starting from time 0 and then directly aligned. Do not use zero padding, looping playback, or implicit truncation to cover up the missing frames.

These are the implementation details of the entry. Do not infer from this that the GMR evaluation of the paper also uses the same script or has the same issues. The `inspect_motion.py` in this chapter only supports the NPZ/ZIP structure mentioned earlier; it cannot directly read the GMR PKL. The export adapter should also verify the units, joint names, quaternions, and timestamps before being used in the common viewer.

## 5. How to extend the other three baselines

| Expansion route | What can be reused | What still needs confirmation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GVHMR → NMR | The same GVHMR human estimation | Converting world-system human parameters into NMR-accepting coordinates, poses, and frame rates |
| WHAM → GMR | The same original video, as well as the target robot for GMR | The adaptation between WHAM human representation and GMR SMPL-X input |
| WHAM → NMR | The same WHAM human estimation | Semantic adaptation of SMPL/SMPL-X, joint dimensions, coordinates, and time axis |

[NMR Official Entry](https://github.com/NJU3DV-HumanoidGroup/MakeTrackingEasy) Accepts human motion files, but does not directly accept RGB videos. The `/predict` on the official Space of核查日 also requires action files. Running the NMR with any AMASS example works, but it can only verify the redirector; it cannot be called "GVHMR → NMR comparison of the same video".

For inputs that have been correctly converted, execute in the NMR environment:

```bash
python inference.py --src /absolute/path/person_motion.npz --output-dir /absolute/path/runs/comparison/nmr
```

NMR documents distinguish the Z-up AMASS field `trans/root_orient/pose_body` from the Y-up standard field `transl/global_orient/body_pose`; the output bmimic NPZ is **50 FPS**. Coordinate conversion cannot be achieved merely by renaming keys, nor can 50 FPS be pieced together with individual frames to a 30 FPS video. After adaptation verification, resampling should be performed along a common second-level time axis, quaternions should use appropriate rotation interpolation, and the original output should be retained. [ Source: NMR input/output instructions ](https://github.com/NJU3DV-HumanoidGroup/MakeTrackingEasy/blob/ba87ad6541f6512df9a370acdd2c2d95da7ae419/README.md)

The official video entry for WHAM is `python demo.py --video /absolute/path/person_6s.mp4 --visualize`, but the generation of human results does not mean that GMR/NMR has been connected. This page does not verify the WHAM adapter, nor provides the fictional `wham_to_robot.py` one-click command. [ Source: WHAM official repository ](https://github.com/yohanshin/WHAM)

## 6. How to make the comparison video and metrics fair

First, create a synchronized video of "original video + the same G1 using five methods"; then use the same controller for dynamic tracking. The demonstration of the eight robots should be presented separately, without mixing with the G1 method rankings.

| Conditions to be fixed | Specific requirements |
| --- | --- |
| Input | The same original file and hash, the same cropping, resolution, start and end time, and frame rate; retain failed segments |
| Ontology | Same G1 joint set, model scale, and constraints; check the quality, collisions, and joint arrangement of models from different repositories |
| Time and coordinates | Retain timestamps; unify meters/radians, world axes, root orientation, and quaternions; record resampling and fixed alignment transformations |
| Image | Same perspective, camera distance, ground level, and playback speed; retain full motion, and side views can be used to observe depth |
| Post-processing | Record the original and recommended post-processing for each method; additional unified filtering results are listed separately |
| Physical execution | Same tracking controller, weights, step size, gain, initial state, and termination criteria; report the number of failures |
| Time consumption | Separate records for detection, human recovery, redirection/direct prediction, post-processing, and rendering using the same hardware; network queueing is listed separately |

When aligning, you cannot arbitrarily translate or rotate each frame to eliminate root trajectory errors; indicators for shape/rigid body alignment must be strictly followed according to their definitions, and the playback that shows global drift should also be retained.

When there is no motion fidelity, qualitative comparisons with clear annotations, joint restriction checks, or jointly defined proxy metrics can be performed. The MAMPJPE/RTE of a paper cannot be directly calculated from the input video alone. For foot slips, the same support annotations or pre-established common judgment rules should be used; each method should not arbitrarily remove the "bad" support frames. Static output may be smooth, but low jitter must be considered together with motion fidelity.

The current six-second input has only **180 frames**, which is less than the 200-frame window required for the paper's Fail metric, and also insufficient for the 600-frame segment used in the paper's physical execution evaluation. The online demonstration also limits it to a maximum of 10 seconds, so this six-second example cannot be directly applied to the failure or success rate of the paper test set.

## 7. Conclusion on Suitable Tutorials

The advantage of being able to explain clearly is that the author achieves better error and execution results in the same G1 visual input task; it directly targets robot learning, providing a way to reduce the error transmission from human body estimation to redirection. Contact correction helps improve physical rationality, but there is a trade-off between accuracy and stability.

Next, first complete the GVHMR → GMR for the same video, and then learn about learning-based redirection and another human body estimator. At that time, local scores and the paper table should be separated, keeping track of wins, draws, and losses. The eight ontology support list should also follow the fixed versions of each item; for example, **Galaxea R1 Pro and Unitree R1 are different robots**, so they cannot be considered as being supported together just because both contain "R1".
